newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate leader puts down some budget markers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate leader puts down some budget markers.

text.p: Senate Majority leader Trent Lott put down some markers on Tuesday for the Clinton administration to hit in putting together a plan to balance the federal budget.
The Mississippi Republican told reporters that the administration needed to tackle the problem of the rapidly-depleting Medicare trust fund head-on and not duck it.
"That would be a total cop-out," Lott said, adding that he does not expect President Clinton to follow that course. "I don't think they will refuse to address the problem," he said.
The Medicare trust fund, which helps pay for health care for the elderly, is set to go bankrupt by the year 2001.

Lott indicated that he expects the administration to propose bigger savings for Medicare than the $124 billion it had called for previously. But he warned against achieving savings in the hospital trust fund by juggling accounts.
"I have the impression that maybe they (the administration) are going to move up in their proposed numbers on Medicare," Lott said. "But it is important ... that it not be a shell game."
Lott said the policies adopted to put Medicare's finances in order were as important as the actual savings achieved.
The Senate leader also warned the administration against proposing a balanced budget plan that envisages government discretionary spending first rising, then falling.
"If you allow the spending to go up in the next two or three years, and then it starts going down, the question is, 'Will it ever go down?'" Lott said.
By law, the administration must submit its budget to Congress by Feb. 3.
But the White House said on Monday it wants to delay issuing its new budget until after President Clinton unveils his second-term agenda in his State of the Union address, tentatively set for Feb. 5.
Lott said he would prefer to have the budget earlier in order to have more time to review Clinton's proposals. But he added, "We will work with him on it any way we can."
